# Provider settings in the assembled application

Released v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f` is the immutable reference. The external observer imports its actual application, verifies all 77 Python modules against that commit, and drives registered navigation/record/cancel actions and real GTK controls. It replaces no handler, factory, scheduler or result. The [independent observations](released-application-providers.json), SHA-256 `b8ec9a4f2084f06224231f70dd60e856cd5b8baad6e659423a72ae18f6bbcb4f`, contain six fresh-session workflows, twenty states and twelve layouts. Recollecting with a fixed private HTTP port for pixels produced byte-identical observations.

`make linux-provider-settings-test` now runs those six native scenarios through the assembled application harness: flow/wide at 1060×780, minimum at 420×520, and narrow/details/error at 480×640. These are content dimensions; GTK's surrounding CSS borders are included in the captured surfaces. A focused replay is `bash linux/tests/run_application_smoke.sh providers flow`. It uses the existing private application runner and its native Codex, keyring and PCM peers. The ordinary fifteen-workflow/143-state application run remains separate and unchanged.

The comparison caught a production error: successful Apply passed an empty catalog to the compact rewrite picker's failed-refresh method, showing “Could not load models” despite a successful save. The root now resets the catalog and reapplies its current configuration without manufacturing a discovery result. The first full native flow fails at `native-saved.inline` in `tmp/native-providers-first-flow.log`; the repaired flow passes all thirteen states in `tmp/native-providers-fixed-flow.log`. The immutable source and fixture were not changed to accommodate that mismatch.

The 295-line Python `provider_settings_smoke.py`, its Make loop and runner branch are retired. It had no shared helper consumers. Its contracts map to these existing or stronger owners:

| Retired contract | Native owner and observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Default routes and no automatic discovery | Fresh assembled application, unchanged largest-Qwen default, no catalog request before Refresh |
| Native model, Fast, effort and local model persistence | Actual Codex catalog, Apply, persisted and active config, service readiness and inline picker; Whisper Tiny replaces the retired test's Whisper Small identity under the authorized three-model limit |
| Independent speech/rewrite catalogs and manual aliases | Eight real HTTP GET requests across the scenarios, capability filtering, retained model pairs and separate effort/key-variable values; no speech upload or rewrite turn |
| Reset of a pending compact catalog | Real held Codex `model/list`, provider Apply and acknowledged child/workspace cleanup before releasing the endpoint; no substituted loading callback |
| Failed discovery, invalid URL and busy Apply | Actual HTTP 401, retained/offline aliases, secret-free controlled notice, unchanged config bytes after invalid URL and during a real PCM recording; cancellation then permits the same draft to save |
| Late discovery and reopening | Held compatible catalog arrives after switching to Codex; saved choices and reopened page remain unchanged by that response |
| Small-window controls and scrolling | Twelve exact released layouts and full-window captures, expanded connection details, error states and reachable Apply at the bottom |
| Scalar provider/setup, credential and local language policies | Existing [provider form owner](provider-pages-evidence.md), [capture settings owner](capture-preferences-evidence.md) and capture/model control comparison retain their distinct coverage |

Only the loopback address is normalized in the state fixture. Displayed URLs use the same fixed port inside separate network namespaces, so all twelve complete native images match their released counterparts with **zero differing pixels**, without masking. Final raw screenshots and the comparison receipt are under `tmp/native-providers-reference-final-<case>-evidence/`, `tmp/native-providers-reference-ack-flow-evidence/`, `tmp/application/run.MDykdO/<case>/` and `tmp/native-providers-final-pixels.log`. The top/bottom snapshots use the real preferences scroller and exact control bounds. GTK 4.22.4, Pango 1.58.2, scale 1, disabled animations/cursor blinking and the same application theme are recorded. Final review strengthened both observers to wait for the held external response to finish before sampling the late-result guard; the independently recollected fixture remains byte-identical.

Both versions use a synthetic external keyring and native Codex process; HTTP authorization is observed only as presence/absence. All eight requests are catalog GETs and both Codex processes only initialize/list models. No History row or clipboard change is permitted. The cancelled recorder is an actual separate PCM process and all owned recorder/Codex processes and temporary workspaces must disappear before shutdown completes. Sparse pinned model/runtime files exercise local readiness only; they prove neither download success nor inference. Existing provisioning and real-model evidence retains its separate scope.

The released compact picker retains its loading annotation when changing only the speech provider cancels an inline model refresh; switching the rewrite route subsequently resets it. This bounded quirk is preserved in the independent state comparison. Default Qwen remains `qwen3-1.7b`; only `whisper-tiny` and `parakeet-v3` are also offered. No retired model is added back.

The old Make target fails at a positively verified interpreter trap in `tmp/native-providers-before.log`. The actual replacement Make target passes all six scenarios with `/usr/bin/python3` and `uv` blocked, with neither trap used, in `tmp/native-providers-final-make.log`; its outer session is `tmp/native-providers-final-make-evidence/session.JvqG0H/`. The shared bounded HTTP peer now supports catalog GET alongside its existing speech multipart and rewrite SSE routes; no second maintained catalog service or interpreter helper is introduced.

The broader application comparison passes fifteen workflows/143 states and its command/settings owner. Affected siblings also pass: 77 capture/model observations, 47 provider transactions/290 GTK states, seventeen preference transactions/132 states, six capture-factory transactions/eight states, and 46 capture transactions/218 states plus three native faults. Logs are `tmp/native-providers-siblings-repeat.log`, with root application session `tmp/application/run.MgPSzX/session.fZLkBs/` and sibling session `tmp/native-providers-siblings-repeat-evidence/session.TE1BEL/`.

An initial broader run failed the existing command-palette `settings-escape` assertion: the native app returned to Capture rather than remaining in Settings. The unchanged repeat passes. A fresh observer of the immutable release records mapped Settings-button focus before and after Escape and reproduces the entire original sixteen-state fixture byte-for-byte. The native intermittent result remains unresolved; no command assertion, reference fixture or keyboard handler is changed. Failure and independent replay evidence remain in `tmp/native-providers-siblings.log` and `tmp/native-providers-command-focus.log`. This is an open acceptance limitation, not a claimed repair or waived failure.

Final `make test` passes 139 tests, zero failures and 68 ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy configurations, formatting and generated-document consistency. Relevant ignored desktop tests run explicitly above. `make linux-python-test` passes 571 tests, Ruff and formatting for 154 remaining files. Full ShellCheck and diff checks pass. Final logs are `tmp/native-providers-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-providers-final-python.log` and `tmp/native-providers-reviewed-gates.log`; the gate session is `tmp/native-providers-reviewed-gates-evidence/session.o9B23Z/`. Existing narrow GtkText allocation, transient accessibility and PyGObject deprecation warnings remain visible. No hosted CI is used.

Substantial review separates the production repair (+7/−1 lines), Make/runner tooling (+19/−13), tests/support (+446/−308) and independently collected JSON (+4,349 lines/168,374 bytes); documentation is separate. The 371-line root observer owns actual configuration, transport, process and geometry evidence that the retired 295-line Python script obtained partly through substituted factories/state. Existing scalar control tests retain their distinct owners. The catalog reset is used by the real application, with no test-only production API. No maintained Python helper is added.

HOME/XDG, display, clipboard, session/accessibility buses, network/PID/mount namespaces are private. Physical input/audio/GPU devices and the system bus are masked. There is no host input, microphone, managed credential, user-content upload or installed-app modification. Complete provisioning through the pages, all joined capture/Meeting/image/Command/Notes workflows, remaining Python/tooling removal, clean distribution, platform/device acceptance and current performance measurements remain required. All whole-workflow parity rows remain Pending; the installed app/widget remain v1.6.0 and the full Rust goal remains active.
